why:
Refuted on two independent grounds, though the underlying field really is absent.

(1) THE CLAIMED EVIDENCE IS FALSE. `grep -ran blockedMarketplaces packages apps` does NOT return 0 on this tree — it returns 5 files: packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js, apps/electron/dist/resources/{pi-agent-server,session-mcp-server}/index.js, apps/electron/resources/{pi-agent-server,session-mcp-server}/index.js. All five are gitignored build bundles (.gitignore:7 `dist`, :12 `apps/electron/resources/pi-agent-server/`), and in them the identifier appears exactly twice, both inside zod `.describe()` strings of a vendored upstream settings schema, with no property read anywhere. So the CONCLUSION ("no Nessy reader") survives, but the proof offered for it does not — and an absence claim whose grep is wrong is not a verified absence.

(2) IT IS A RECORDED, DATED, REASONED DEVIATION — not a discovery. Three places already carry it:
  - docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-marketplace-entry-authority.md:232, in a section titled "## 6. `plugin-marketplaces.md` rows we do not implement", whose preamble states each row was "Verified against the page as fetched 2026-07-29, not copied from the sweep. Each row was checked in the tree before it was written down."
  - docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:184 (generated from that plan's category string).
  - docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:696, which already inventories `blockedMarketplaces` among the ~15 managed-only keys under R25.
  The recorded reason, verbatim: "S9 implements the allowlist only. On a managed fleet the allowlist is the stronger control, since anything unlisted is already refused, so the blocklist adds reach not safety." Per AGENTS.md, a plan is where a deviation's reason lives and the register harvests it — this is a decision with a reason, the same species as the inert-worklist §3 rows, not a defect.

(3) THE CONSEQUENCE AS PHRASED IS OVERSTATED — the "one layer up" check. `RegistrySourceService.isSourceAllowed` (packages/shared/src/marketplace/registry-source.ts:388-393) evaluates `strictKnownMarketplaces` before any network or filesystem operation, carrying the comment citing `plugins/org.md#how-entries-match (was line 762 of the retired plugin-marketplaces page)` — i.e. the allowlist half already has the exact "checked before downloading, so they never touch the filesystem" timing the quoted sentence attributes to the blocklist, and it is wired end-to-end (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:295-306 → registry-source.ts:390). With an allowlist set, an admin blocks a source by not listing it. The only case `blockedMarketplaces` uniquely covers is "no allowlist at all, block one named source" — a strictly weaker posture than the control we do implement. Additionally, "has no denylist field" is wrong as stated: ManagedPiPolicyV1 carries `deniedPluginKeys` (managed-policy.ts:84, enforced :1518) and `deniedMcpServers` (:130). What is absent is a marketplace-SOURCE denylist specifically — naming the policy denylist-free is the sibling-subsystem error.

Not a rebrand/subscription/gateway product difference, and not one of the nine inert-worklist §3 owner decisions (those are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) — but it is the equivalent recorded decision in the deviation register.

Honest residue: the field genuinely does not exist in ManagedPiPolicyV1, and an admin who deliberately runs WITHOUT `strictKnownMarketplaces` cannot block one named source. That gap is real, already logged, and rated reach-not-safety by the owner.
correctedState:
`blockedMarketplaces` is a managed-only key (permissions.md:499, "### Managed-only settings" table) that Nessy does not implement — a known, dated, reasoned omission, not an unrecorded divergence.

What exists: ManagedPiPolicyV1 carries `strictKnownMarketplaces` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:141, parsed :1428-1431, :1448) and `extraKnownMarketplaces` (:158). The allowlist is enforced at MarketplaceRegistrySourceService.isSourceAllowed (packages/shared/src/marketplace/registry-source.ts:388-393) via isManagedMarketplaceAllowed (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-marketplace-entries.ts:612-616), before any network or filesystem operation — matching plugins/org.md#how-entries-match (was line 762 of the retired plugin-marketplaces page) — and is wired from packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:295-306. A delivered (`extraKnownMarketplaces`) source passes the same gate and cannot widen the narrowing; a refusal surfaces as `refused-by-allowlist` (registry-source.ts:374-377).

Related denylists that DO exist, and their scope: `deniedPluginKeys` (managed-policy.ts:84, validated :1293, enforced :1518 as exact `.includes(pluginKey)` with no wildcard) and `deniedMcpServers` (:130). Neither can express "block this marketplace source" — `deniedPluginKeys` denies individual `plugin@marketplace` keys only.

Grep truth: `blockedMarketplaces` appears in 5 gitignored build bundles (pi-agent-server and session-mcp-server dist output) purely as upstream zod `.describe()` text with no consumer; zero occurrences in tracked TypeScript source.

Recorded decision: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-marketplace-entry-authority.md:232 (§6 "rows we do not implement", page-verified 2026-07-29) → docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:184; also inventoried at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:696 and discussed at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-phase4-findings.md:242-248. Rationale on record: the allowlist is the stronger control since anything unlisted is already refused, so the blocklist adds reach, not safety. Same section also records `disableSideloadFlags` as unimplemented.

Residual real gap (already accepted): an administrator who sets no `strictKnownMarketplaces` cannot block one named marketplace source.
